etymologies.etymologyHTML: From employ +‎ -er, first attested in the late 16th century. Compare French employeur.

definitions.definition: A person, firm or other entity which pays for or hires the services of another person.

quote.citation: 1897 December (indicated as 1898), Winston Churchill, chapter X, in The Celebrity: An Episode, New York, N.Y.: The Macmillan Company; London: Macmillan & Co., Ltd., →OCLC:
quote.text: The skipper Mr. Cooke had hired at Far Harbor was a God-fearing man with a luke warm interest in his new billet and employer, and had only been prevailed upon to take charge of the yacht after the offer of an emolument equal to half a year's sea pay of an ensign in the navy.

quote.citation: 1973, E. F. Schumacher, Small is Beautiful:
quote.text: the ideal from the point of view of the employer is to have output without employees, and the ideal from the point of view of the employee is to have income without employment.
